issues.failure_explanation: There is no Polish parameter space with a jointly Borel evaluation relation that uniformly represents every Borel subset or every Borel function of an uncountable Polish space; such a universal Borel relation would impose a bounded Borel rank on all sections. Standard well-founded Borel codes do not form a Polish space with the asserted Borel evaluation and measure maps. Thus the proposed Borel witness set B, and hence analyticity of A_{z_0}, are not established. In addition, B is defined over all continuous F without imposing the nonsingularity condition defining Omega_X^infinity.

issues.failure_explanation: The local greedy choice of a star need not maximize the eventual or even fixed-level number of stars. For example, let S contain the full subtree below the first bit 0 and only the single branch 1000... below the first bit 1. Then S contains the Silver tree obtained by fixing the first bit to 0 and leaving all later coordinates free. Nevertheless the greedy rule chooses a star at level 1, then is forced to choose 0 at every later coordinate so that both surviving prefixes remain in S; its star count stays one. Thus S in V does not imply unbounded k_m(S), invalidating the forward spectral implication.

issues.failure_explanation: Small lower norms for a sequence of different blocks do not imply proximity to any block's approximate point spectrum. A Koopman counterexample is obtained from disjoint finite blocks X_N={0,...,N}, each with positive atomic measure, and F_N(j)=min(j+1,N). Every finite-dimensional block Koopman operator has approximate point spectrum {0,1}. For any fixed 0<|lambda|<1, however, f_N(j)=lambda^j has norm one and block residual only at j=N, of size |1-lambda||lambda|^N. In the L-infinity product these vectors show lambda is an approximate eigenvalue of the global operator, although lambda is not in the closure of the union {0,1}.
